KEY MESSAGE 1...A strengthening storm system organizes off the 
northern Mid-Atlantic coast Thursday into Friday.

A vigorous upper-level trough continues to be forecast to 
evolve across the eastern U.S. later this week and into the 
weekend. This supports a surface low that strengthens as it 
tracks across portions of the Mid-Atlantic and then especially 
just offshore of the Northeast. It appears that low pressure 
will tend to consolidate off the New Jersey coast on Thursday, 
then deepen as it tracks north-northeast toward the Canadian 
Maritimes Friday into Saturday. While there are still some 
differences with the handling of the embedded short waves, there
is better model clustering with the surface low 
placement/track. Overall, it will be unsettled across our region
as we go through Thursday and Friday.

The strength of the parent upper-level trough results in a 
colder air mass moving in with time, however the initial air 
mass is not all that cold (the lack of a cold antecedent air 
mass). As the surface low consolidates off the northern Mid-
Atlantic coast, the winds will turn more out of the northwest 
and this will increase the cold air advection. This will result 
in some colder air seeping southeastward later Thursday night 
but especially Friday into Friday night. The air mass may become
sufficiently cold enough mostly across our far northwestern 
zones for a rain/snow mix or even some snow across the higher 
elevations, confined particularly to the Pocono Plateau. Any
snowfall accumulation is expected to be less than an inch. Some
elevated locations across the Lehigh Valley and Northwestern NJ
may see a few wet flakes mixing in, but no accumulations are
expected. Otherwise, a rain event is forecast. The amount of 
precipitation (rain and/or snow) will depend on the ultimate 
track of the surface low and whether a deformation zones wraps 
back into our northern to central areas. At the moment, rainfall
amounts north of the PA Turnpike to I-195 corridor range around
the 0.75-1.25" range while further south across Philly and 
south, we are expecting less than 0.75" of rainfall, with less 
than 0.25" expected for the southern Delmarva.

The model consensus looks to be more of a northward positioning
of the surface low, which if this ends up occurring would 
result in less rainfall with a southward extent across our area.
The coastal impacts, including the potential for stronger 
onshore winds and also (minor) tidal flooding, are a little less
certain because the surface low track right over our area would
lessen the residence time of the (stronger) onshore flow. Prior
to the low fully consolidating offshore, some elevated 
instability could get into especially portions of our coastal 
plain and therefore a rumble of thunder is possible later 
Thursday night and Friday morning. The strongest winds with this
look to occur as the storm moves farther away and the cold air 
advection then increases from the northwest. The main 
uncertainty is on how much precipitation occurs with this event 
region-wide and the extent/amount of any higher elevation snow 
(mainly for the southern Poconos). 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Minor tidal flooding expected with Thursday 
Morning's high tide.

A brief period of onshore flow will result in some elevated
tides. For the most part, tidal flooding will be relatively
spotty for communities along the Atlantic Ocean and Delaware
Bay. More widespread tidal flooding though is currently forecast
for Barnegat Bay, which could result in some inundation of low
lying areas and roadways Thursday Morning. As a result, a
Coastal Flood Advisory was issued for Ocean County. 

No other headlines are in place nor expected. No tidal flooding
is expected along the tidal Delaware River and Chesapeake Bay. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...A stretch of below normal temperatures begins 
on Friday, continuing through the weekend as a much colder 
airmass moves overhead.

In the wake of the storm, as it deepens and tracks toward the 
Canadian Maritimes over the weekend, a colder air mass will be 
in place across our area. In addition, a tightened pressure 
gradient coupled with deeper mixing will result in a period of 
breezy to windy conditions over the weekend. The strongest winds
look to occur on Saturday, with peak gusts to about 35 mph, 
then while still gusty on Sunday it appears the speeds come down
a little. Daytime temperatures on Friday and Saturday should 
not get out of the 40s for many areas, with temperatures at 
night dropping into the 20s to low 30s. Where the growing season
is still active across Delmarva, parts of southern New Jersey 
and far southeastern Pennsylvania. There could even be some lake
effect snow and/or rain showers into the southern Poconos on 
Saturday. 

Temperatures start to moderate a bit Sunday through Tuesday. 
Despite that, high temperatures are only in the upper 40s to low
50s each day which is still below average for this time of 
year.
